name: Raymond Zell Simons
notable_stories: Eloped with Dradie Kulp to Ritzville in 1915
He later worked in real estate and convinced several Kulp relatives to relocate to the Tri-Cities area
Founded the Chetzamoka Park Zoo on the Columbia River waterfront (Pasco area)
Ray and Dradie celebrated their 50th wedding anniversary at the Pasco Grange
Eloped with Dradie Kulp to Ritzville; real estate developer who named streets in Pasco after family
Grandpa Ray Simons had a bout with tuberculosis, which is why they sold their Lynden farm and moved to the drier climate of Pasco, Washington in the 1950s (John's memoir — 'My Grandparents' chapter).
Ray founded the Chetzamoka Park Zoo by rescuing unwanted animals from zoos in Seattle, Portland, and Spokane.
Ray named streets in the Pasco area after family members. 'Glen Acres' is a residential development named after Beryl's brother Glen.
John's last vivid memory of Ray: mid-1970s, obviously suffering from dementia when he visited John's family in Olympia.
Ray passed away not long after the mid-1970s visit (confirmed consistent with death 7 May 1977).

His grandson Steve Simons, aged about 8 to 10, drove Ray’s pickup into Pasco with his cousin John Adams to collect discarded grocery-store food for the zoo animals, with blocks on the pedals and looking under the steering wheel. [John Howard Adams, A Memoir, text lines 190–193, 616–619]
C-005: WWI Draft Card — Birth: June 14, 1897, Michigan. Consistent with canonical.
1900 Census: Raymond Simons, age 2 (born ~1897-98). Siblings listed: Ettie, Lola, Bertha.
1920 Census — Raymond's own household: Raymond Simons (22), Dradie Simons (21), Elaine Simons (1). Elaine born ~1919.
1930 Census: Raymond and Dradie with multiple children; Elmer Kulp (Dradie's brother) present.
Simons, McPhail, and Kulp families were located within a few farms of each other prior to marriage.
John's first memory of Ray is of him chasing John's father around the farmyard with a pair of pants smeared with cow manure that George Sr. had tricked him into sitting on.
milestones: Registered for the WWI draft while working in Milton, Oregon
Moved his family from the Lynden farm to Pasco, Washington, in the 1950s
Moved family from Lynden to Pasco due to tuberculosis diagnosis
Military: Raymond Zell Simons registered for the WWI draft on 26 Aug 1918 at Blaine, Whatcom County, giving birth 14 June 1897 at South Haven, Michigan and father's birthplace Indiana.
Ray's Pasco farm had about half a mile of Columbia River waterfront, bought before the Hanford Nuclear Reservation was built; the land became valuable as the area grew. (1950s)
Late in life Ray and Dradie moved into a nursing home, and the farmland was sold. (late 1970s)
Registered for the WWII draft on 16 Feb 1942 at Kennewick, Washington; self-employed, with his brother-in-law Dan Groves as next of kin
Buried at Desert Lawn Memorial Park, Kennewick, Washington
education: Completed the second year of high school (1940 census).
career: In 1918 Ray Simons was employed by Will Steen in Milton, Oregon.
Ray sold real estate in Pasco and persuaded several Kulp families to move there. (abt 1954)
Farmer: a rented farm at Lynden in 1920, his own farm near Richland in 1940, and a farm in Franklin County in 1950.
School bus driver in Delta, Whatcom County, in 1930.
locations: Covert Township, Van Buren County, Michigan

notes: New story: named streets in Pasco after family members.
NEW: tuberculosis is confirmed reason for Lynden→Pasco move. Source: John's memoir.
Ray Simons's draft card describes him with blue eyes and dark brown hair. [Family research emails, email 50]

Open question: Irma writes that Ray and Dradie were 'neighbors in 1920' but means 1910; they were married by the 1920 census. The elopement to Ritzville is dated Dec 1915, when Dradie was 17 [Family research emails, email 17, 23, 50]
Late in life Ray and Dradie moved into a nursing home, and the farmland was sold. [John Howard Adams, A Memoir, text line 594]

Born 14 Jun 1897 at South Haven, Michigan, as his WWI and WWII draft cards, Washington death record and Social Security record all agree; the Ann Arbor birthplace comes from his Tri-City Herald obituary. He died 7 May 1977 at Kennewick while living in Pasco (Washington death certificate 9562). The Raymond Simons who died in Seattle in 1976 was a different man.
His Washington death record names his parents as Aaron Simons and Hattie Micheals.
Censuses give his father's birthplace as Ohio (1900, 1910), Iowa (1920) and Illinois (1930), and his own as Washington in 1930.

In 1930 the household at Buffalo Road, Delta, included Dradie's brother Elmer Kulp; in 1940 his daughter Elaine, her husband Les Rinehart and their children Jerry and Janet lived with him near Richland.
CORRECTION: his WWI draft card is dated 26 Aug 1918 (the registration of men who had turned 21 since June 1918; Ray turned 21 on 14 Jun 1918), not 11 Sep 1918.
